faq.a: Gulten is associated with the Turkish form غُولْتِن, whose core sense is gulten; rose body (turkish).

faq.q: What is the origin of Gulten?
faq.a: Gulten is associated with Turkish. Gulten is Turkish, from gül ('rose') + ten ('body, skin'), used as a female given name.
No — the underlying form is Turkish, not Arabic.
Gulten can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkish-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Gulten should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Gülten is a Turkish compound, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Gulten mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Gulten is rendered گل تن and carries the sense گل تن، گلاب جیسا بدن.

faq.q: What does Gulten mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Gulten is rendered گلتن and carries the sense گلتن، تن گل.
A romanized syllable approximation is gul-ten. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Gulten?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Gulten, gulten. Script forms are غُولْتِن, ګلتن, گل تن, گلتن, गुलतेन.

faq.q: Is Gulten a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
